newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X says winding down operations in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says winding down operations in Indonesia.

text.p: Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Friday it was winding down Indonesian operations, ending a tumultuous chapter that began with its 1993 purchase of the now-worthless Busang property.
"We are winding down all our activities, that includes gold and copper exploration activities in Aceh and North Sulawesi," Bre-X financial officer Bernhard Leode told Reuters.
He said exploration in Aceh, on northern Sumatra island, and on northern Sulawesi island had been carried out by Bre-X affiliates Bresea Resources Ltd and Bro-X Minerals
Bresea, which owns 22.7 percent of Bro-X and 22.3 percent of Bre-X, and Bro-X were awarded contracts of work last month by the government to explore for and develop mines.

The Busang project -- once estimated by Bre-X to contain some 70 million ounces of gold, making it the biggest gold find this century -- collapsed after an independent audit found insignificant amounts of gold in the property in East Kalimantan province on Borneo island.
Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd, which did the audit, also found that Busang data had been falsified on an unprecedented scale, making it the biggest mining fraud in history.

Indonesian police and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the Busang scandal, which led to the delisting of Bre-X from the Toronto Stock Exchange, where its stock was once worth over C$6 billion.
Indonesia has frozen all activities of Bre-X and its subsidiaries in the country until the probe is completed.
Bre-X's Leode said the company hoped to raise money from its winding down of Indonesian operations by possibly selling its assets, which included cars, machinery and office equipment.
"There's not much to sell. We have some heavy equipment, cars and computers worth about $750,000 if there are buyers," he said.
He said investments made by the Bre-X group totalled some $30 million since beginning operations in 1993.
Bre-X chief executive David Walsh gambled with the company's last C$10,000 to visit Indonesia in 1993 to take an option on the Busang property.

"At that time Bre-X was down to its last C$10,000 which I spent on coming over here," Walsh said in an interview in Jakarta last February. "Our other explorations have been zero. I had never imagined it (Busang) would be this big."
Meanwhile, Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana was quote as saying in the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper on Friday that ministry secretary-general Umar Said would be replaced.
He said the move was not linked to the Busang scandal.
"This is a normal replacement. There is no link to Busang," he was quoted as saying on Thursday.
The ministry's director-general of mining, Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, was replaced early last month. Both Kuntoro and Said played a leading role in the Busang saga.
